# Executive Summary

- **The requested analyses have been completed without removing samples.** Juliane's
  revised Excel table was used as the authoritative metadata source for all 73 samples
  from 72 patients. The internal `PM` label is displayed as **non-IBM IIM, NOS**.
- **The methylation data contain strong disease-group-associated structure, but the
  study design does not allow that structure to be attributed to disease alone.**
  Disease group, Sentrix, source/city, biopsy site, age, and sex are structurally
  overlapping. Source and Sentrix cannot be adjusted jointly with disease group in a
  full model because those designs are rank deficient.
- **The main unsupervised observation can remain, with narrower wording.** PCA and
  many t-SNE settings preserve group-associated structure, but exact t-SNE geometry
  varies and the weakest clinically relevant comparison is ALS versus non-ALS NMA.
  These are pilot, association-level findings rather than proof of disease-specific
  molecular entities or clinical diagnostic performance.
- **Several answers still require Juliane's clinical knowledge.** Archive case
  selection, slide/clinical review, the definition of `lymphomonocytes`, and the
  availability of validated tissue-composition/pathology measures cannot be answered
  from the analytical files and have not been guessed.

::: {.reader-guide}
<div class="box-title">How to use this report</div>

Each analytical section follows the same path: **reviewer concern → Juliane's email
or agreed team direction → completed response → interpretation and manuscript
consequence**. Red boxes summarize the concern, blue boxes record the decision,
green boxes describe completed work, and yellow boxes identify text or facts that
still need Juliane's decision.
:::

# 1. The metadata are complete for analysis, but not for every clinical question

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Relevant reviewer concerns</div>

Reviewer 1 requested coloring and adjustment by dataset source, Sentrix/chip, age,
sex, biopsy site, inflammatory-cell fraction, fiber type, denervation, fibrosis,
necrosis, and pathology severity. Reviewer 2 separately asked how archive cases were
selected and whether cellular composition was addressed by deconvolution or stated
as a major limitation.
:::

::: {.decision-box}
<div class="box-title">Juliane's email and agreed team direction</div>

Use the categories in Juliane's new Excel table. Retain all 73 samples; there are no
additional samples and no disease-group reassignment. Display `PM` as **non-IBM IIM,
NOS**. Do not assign a biological meaning to the `lymphomonocytes` low/medium/high
categories without a definition from the clinical team.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed analytical response</div>

All `r nrow(meta)` metadata rows map uniquely to 73 methylation samples from
`r length(unique(meta$patient_id))` patients. Sentrix ID and array position match the
sample key. Dataset source was explicitly assigned as MALICoT for controls, GEO
GSE121961 for Multiminicores, and in-house data for the remaining samples.
:::

The `lymphomonocytes` field is reproduced exactly as supplied and used only as a
descriptive annotation. It is not interpreted and is not included as an adjustment
covariate. Validated macrophage fraction, fiber-type estimates, denervation score,
fibrosis, necrosis, and pathology-severity measures were not supplied; they were not
invented or imputed.

::: {.decision-needed-box}
<div class="box-title">Juliane decision needed</div>

Please provide the clinical wording for: the total archive candidates and exclusions;
whether all cases in the eight-year interval were reviewed; whether slides and
clinical information were reassessed; how differences between diagnosing
pathologists were handled; what `lymphomonocytes` means; and why the requested
validated tissue-composition/pathology estimates are unavailable. The analysis can
support a major-limitation statement, but cannot supply these facts.
:::

# 2. Recoloring shows why disease and confounding cannot be separated visually

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer concern</div>

The near-complete separation is unexpectedly strong for 73 heterogeneous,
non-neoplastic muscle samples. The reviewer asked whether the same PCA and t-SNE
coordinates align with source, batch, age, sex, biopsy site, or tissue composition.
:::

::: {.decision-box}
<div class="box-title">Juliane's proposed response</div>

Display the categories in the supplied Excel file on the existing PCA and t-SNE
coordinates. Variables that are unavailable or undefined should not be inferred.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed solution</div>

The original unsupervised coordinates were preserved and recolored separately by
disease group, city, Sentrix, age, sex, muscle site, and `lymphomonocytes`. Full
single-variable panels are available in the supplementary-figure folder.
:::

**How to read these figures.** Each panel contains the same samples at the same
coordinates; only the color annotation changes. If a disease cluster is also almost
entirely one source, Sentrix, age group, sex, or biopsy site, the plot cannot tell us
which of those overlapping variables generated the separation. Recoloring diagnoses
the study-design overlap; it does not statistically remove it.

```{r, out.width='100%', fig.show='asis'}
knitr::include_graphics(c(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_unsupervised_PCA.png"),
  file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_unsupervised_tSNE.png")))
```

**Manuscript consequence.** Retain “disease-group-associated methylation structure,”
but avoid “intrinsic,” “disease-specific,” or causal wording. State that technical,
demographic, biopsy-site, and bulk-tissue effects cannot be fully separated.

# 3. PCA confirms strong structure and simultaneously exposes confounding

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer request</div>

Provide a scree plot and cumulative variance, examine several PC pairs, quantify
associations between leading PCs and the supplied variables, compare scaled with
centered-unscaled PCA, and inspect the strongest positive and negative CpG loadings.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed solution</div>

Scaled and centered-unscaled PCA were run on the complete post-QC matrix. The first
20 PCs and cumulative variance, multiple PC projections, PC–metadata association
statistics, and annotated leading loadings were generated. The detailed PC-pair and
loading panels are in the supplementary figures and machine-readable tables.
:::

**How to read the scree plot.** The bars show the fraction of total variation assigned
to each PC; the cumulative line shows how quickly those fractions accumulate. PCA is
not a disease test: it identifies the strongest directions of variation, regardless
of whether their origin is biological, technical, demographic, or compositional.

```{r, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_PCA_scree.png"))
```

**How to read the association map.** The color represents eta-squared: larger values
mean that samples with different metadata categories occupy more distinct positions
along that PC. It is a one-variable association and must not be read as an independent
causal contribution when variables overlap.

```{r, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_PC_metadata_associations.png"))
```

On scaled PC1, disease-group eta-squared is
`r sprintf('%.3f',assoc$eta_squared[assoc$PCA=='scaled' & assoc$PC=='PC1' & assoc$variable=='display_group'])`.
However, Sentrix eta-squared is also
`r sprintf('%.3f',assoc$eta_squared[assoc$PCA=='scaled' & assoc$PC=='PC1' & assoc$variable=='sentrix_id'])`
on PC1 and
`r sprintf('%.3f',assoc$eta_squared[assoc$PCA=='scaled' & assoc$PC=='PC2' & assoc$variable=='sentrix_id'])`
on PC2; city/source and biopsy site also associate with leading PCs. The similar
disease pattern in scaled and unscaled PCA supports the presence of strong structure,
but does not resolve its cause.

::: {.interpretation-box}
<div class="box-title">Interpretation for the manuscript</div>

The correct conclusion is not “PCA validates the disease entities.” It is: **PCA
detects strong group-associated structure, and the same leading components are also
associated with technical and cohort variables that overlap with disease group.**
:::

# 4. t-SNE is broadly suggestive, but its exact map is parameter-dependent

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer request</div>

Explicitly report that the submitted `Rtsne` run used its default internal PCA with
50 dimensions; test `initial_dims` 10, 20, 30, 50, and 72, perplexities 5, 10, 15,
and 20, multiple random seeds, and quantitative stability. Also run `pca=FALSE`
directly on the full probe matrix if feasible.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed solution</div>

The baseline is now described correctly as t-SNE operating after a 50-dimensional
internal centered, unscaled PCA. A grid of `r nrow(sens)` runs tested five initial
dimensions, four perplexities, and ten random seeds. Similarity to the submitted map
was summarized by Procrustes correlation after removing irrelevant rotation,
reflection, and orientation differences.
:::

**Plain-language explanation.** `initial_dims` controls how much PCA information is
given to t-SNE; perplexity controls the approximate neighborhood scale; and the random
seed changes the algorithm's starting arrangement. A Procrustes correlation near 1
means that the samples preserve a very similar relative layout after the two maps are
aligned. A wider or lower box means that the displayed geometry depends more strongly
on random initialization or parameter choice.

```{r, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_tSNE_stability.png"))
```

Across individual runs, Procrustes correlations ranged from
`r sprintf('%.3f',min(sens$procrustes_correlation))` to
`r sprintf('%.3f',max(sens$procrustes_correlation))`. After averaging the ten seeds
within each parameter combination, the range was
`r sprintf('%.3f',min(sens_agg$procrustes_correlation))` to
`r sprintf('%.3f',max(sens_agg$procrustes_correlation))`. Perplexity 20 was generally
the most stable. Disease-group silhouette values remained positive, meaning that
some local group separation persisted, but its strength and exact shape varied.

**The direct full-matrix check addresses the PCA-default question.** With `pca=FALSE`,
t-SNE used the full 771,381-probe input and completed in approximately
`r sprintf('%.2f',tsne_runtime$elapsed_minutes)` minutes. Its Procrustes correlation
with the submitted map was `r sprintf('%.3f',tsne_direct$procrustes_correlation)` and
its disease-group silhouette was `r sprintf('%.3f',tsne_direct$disease_silhouette)`.

```{r, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_tSNE_direct_pca_false.png"))
```

::: {.interpretation-box}
<div class="box-title">Interpretation for the manuscript</div>

Many settings preserve local group-associated structure, so the original pattern is
not a single-seed accident. However, the precise cluster shape, spacing, and relative
placement are not fixed. t-SNE axes and global inter-cluster distances have no direct
biological meaning and should not be used to define disease entities.
:::

# 5. The new correlation heatmap supplies the label-free check requested by the reviewer

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer concern and requested remedy</div>

The original Figure 1F selected CpGs using disease labels, so separation is partly
expected by construction. It cannot serve as independent unsupervised evidence. The
reviewer requested a full-matrix sample correlation heatmap with label-free ordering
and diagnosis/confounders added only after clustering.
:::

::: {.decision-box}
<div class="box-title">Proposed figure decision</div>

Use the new label-free sample correlation heatmap as the main unsupervised heatmap.
Move the original top-CpG heatmap to the supplement, or retain it only with an explicit
“supervised descriptive visualization” label.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed solution</div>

Pearson correlations were calculated between every pair of samples using the complete
post-QC M-value matrix. Hierarchical clustering used `1 − Pearson correlation` without
disease labels. Disease and available metadata were added only as annotations after
the row and column order had been determined.
:::

**How to read the figure.** Blocks of higher sample-to-sample correlation indicate
similar methylation profiles in the original high-dimensional matrix. The annotation
tracks show whether those blocks coincide with disease group, source, Sentrix, or
other supplied variables. Because the ordering is label-free, the heatmap is an
appropriate independent companion to PCA and t-SNE; it still cannot distinguish
disease from perfectly or strongly aligned confounders.

```{r, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_sample_correlation_heatmap.png"))
```

# 6. Subset analyses weaken the broadest claims, especially for ALS versus NMA

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer request</div>

Recompute PCA and t-SNE after excluding MMC, excluding controls, restricting to the
in-house data, comparing IBM with non-IBM IIM, NOS, and comparing ALS with
non-ALS NMA. Do not merely delete points from the full-cohort map, and assess
sensitivity to influential individual samples.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed solution</div>

All five PCA and t-SNE analyses were recomputed independently from each subset. The
summary below reports group-separation silhouette values; higher positive values mean
stronger separation, values near zero mean overlapping groups. Leave-one-out influence
analyses and complete panels are available in the supplementary figures.
:::

```{r}
subs_show<-subs[,c("subset","n","groups","PCA_disease_silhouette","TSNE_disease_silhouette")]
names(subs_show)<-c("Subset","N","Groups","PCA silhouette","t-SNE silhouette")
knitr::kable(subs_show,digits=3)
```

The in-house-data analysis shows weaker separation than the full mixed-source
cohort. ALS versus non-ALS NMA is the weakest clinically focused distinction: PCA
silhouette is `r sprintf('%.3f',subs$PCA_disease_silhouette[subs$subset=='ALS_vs_nonALS_NMA'])`
and t-SNE silhouette is
`r sprintf('%.3f',subs$TSNE_disease_silhouette[subs$subset=='ALS_vs_nonALS_NMA'])`.

::: {.interpretation-box}
<div class="box-title">Manuscript consequence</div>

Describe ALS–NMA findings as **exploratory and hypothesis-generating**, explicitly
cite the six ALS cases, and avoid language implying a validated ALS methylation
signature. The IBM versus non-IBM IIM result may be retained as a pilot association,
with the same confounding and sample-size caveats.
:::

# 7. Differential methylation is sensitive to adjustment and cannot absorb all confounders

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer concern</div>

If unsupervised separation is influenced by confounders, differential methylation,
pathways, label-informed heatmaps, and classifiers may inherit the same structure.
Reviewer 2 additionally requested cell-composition adjustment or an explicit major
limitation if validated deconvolution is not available.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed solution</div>

Differential models were rerun unadjusted, adjusted for age and sex, and adjusted for
biopsy site. Model estimability was audited before interpreting results. The repeated
patient could not support a general within-patient correlation estimate because only
one patient was repeated, so each paired specimen was excluded in turn as a sensitivity
check.
:::

```{r}
audit_show<-audit
names(audit_show)<-c("Model","N","Parameters","Rank","Full rank","Residual df")
knitr::kable(audit_show)
```

Source and Sentrix models are not full rank with disease group. In plain language,
some disease categories and technical/source categories overlap so strongly that the
model cannot estimate separate coefficients for both. Normalization cannot repair
this structural imbalance.

**How to read the sensitivity figure.** The panels compare how many CpGs remain
significant, how strongly effect sizes agree with the unadjusted analysis, and how
many of the top-ranked CpGs are retained. Large changes after adjustment indicate
that the biological interpretation depends on the covariate model.

```{r, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_differential_sensitivity.png"))
```

Biopsy-site adjustment reduced ALS-versus-NMA CpGs at FDR < 0.001 from two to zero.
MMC-versus-control changed especially strongly after age/sex adjustment: significant
CpGs decreased from 103,209 to 531 and top-1,000 overlap was 0.077. Pathway claims
based on unstable CpG sets should therefore be softened and presented as sensitivity-
dependent exploratory findings.

::: {.decision-needed-box}
<div class="box-title">Juliane decision needed</div>

Because no validated cell fractions or pathology scores were supplied, the response
should explicitly identify absent cell-composition adjustment as a **major limitation**
unless Juliane can provide a defensible validated estimate and its provenance.
:::

# 8. Supervised learning remains a research result, not a clinical diagnostic claim

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Relevant reviewer concerns</div>

Reviewer 1 asked whether supervised models inherit source/batch structure. Reviewer 2
objected to “predict a correct diagnosis” and similar language because the outcomes
are study disease groups, not a complete clinical differential diagnosis.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Completed solution</div>

A metadata-only model quantified how much disease-group information is already
contained in the supplied covariates. The methylation workflow was rebuilt with a
patient-aware split so the two specimens from one patient cannot be divided between
training and test sets. The manuscript draft uses “disease group” and avoids “correct
diagnosis,” “entity-specific,” and clinical-classifier wording.
:::

**How to read the metadata-only result.** This is a confounding diagnostic, not an
alternative clinical classifier. If Sentrix/source/demographic metadata predict the
study labels, then a methylation model can obtain high accuracy partly from signals
aligned with those variables.

```{r, out.width='100%'}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(root,"figures/web/Figure_metadata_only_classifier.png"))
```

All available metadata achieved mean repeated-CV balanced accuracy
`r sprintf('%.3f',mean(ml$balanced_accuracy[ml$feature_set=='all_available_metadata']))`;
Sentrix alone achieved
`r sprintf('%.3f',mean(ml$balanced_accuracy[ml$feature_set=='sentrix_only']))`. This
does not prove that the methylation classifier uses only batch, but it demonstrates
that confounding variables contain substantial group information.

The patient-aware logistic-regression model achieved
`r sprintf('%.1f%%',100*pml$accuracy[pml$model=='Logistic regression'])` held-out
accuracy and `r sprintf('%.1f%%',100*pml$balanced_accuracy[pml$model=='Logistic regression'])`
balanced accuracy. These numbers describe one small held-out research cohort; they do
not establish generalization to new institutions, batches, muscle sites, or diseases
outside the six study groups.

::: {.interpretation-box}
<div class="box-title">Manuscript consequence</div>

Report the models as proof-of-concept **study disease-group prediction**. Do not call
the output a correct diagnosis or claim clinical diagnostic performance. Emphasize
patient-aware splitting, structural confounding, small group sizes, and the need for
independent external validation.
:::

The reviewer doubts that the archive contained only six non-IBM IIM, NOS and thirteen

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer 2: cell composition and ALS wording</div>

Either incorporate validated deconvolution estimates or state their absence as a

cases.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Drafted response direction</div>

No unsupported deconvolution has been added. Bulk-tissue and missing cell-composition

:::

::: {.reviewer-box}
<div class="box-title">Reviewer 2: terminology and proofreading</div>

Replace “diagnosis” with “disease group” where appropriate, remove residual
disease-specific overstatement, correct placeholder supplementary references, and
proofread the entire manuscript.
:::

::: {.response-box}
<div class="box-title">Drafted response direction</div>

A clean revised manuscript and point-by-point rebuttal have been generated with
softened terminology. A final author-level proofread remains necessary, especially
for clinical facts, supplementary numbering, authorship wording, and any text Juliane
adds after this analytical revision.
:::

# Recommended decisions and next steps

1. **Approve the central wording:** retain disease-group-associated methylation
   structure as a pilot observation, not proof of disease-specific entities.
2. **Approve the figure strategy:** keep baseline t-SNE, add the label-free correlation
   heatmap as the unsupervised Figure 1 companion, and move/relabel the supervised
   top-CpG heatmap.
3. **Use sensitivity analyses transparently:** place PCA/t-SNE robustness,
   confounder-colored panels, subset analyses, and adjusted differential results in
   the supplement and cite them in the main text.
4. **Keep ALS–NMA exploratory:** name the six-case limitation and avoid diagnostic or
   validation language.
5. **State the unresolved confounding clearly:** source/Sentrix cannot be separated
   statistically from disease group in this cohort; missing validated cell-composition
   estimates are a major limitation.
6. **Supply the clinical facts:** archive screening, selection, slide/clinical review,
   pathology adjudication, and the meaning of `lymphomonocytes` require Juliane's text.
7. **Confirm authorship wording:** Juliane's email records agreement that Joseph can
   be co-last author with equal contribution; confirm the precise author order and
   contribution statement before submission.
8. **Perform a final integrated proofread:** check terminology, cross-references,
   supplementary table/figure numbers, author contributions, and consistency between
   manuscript, legends, tables, and rebuttal.

# Further questions for Juliane

- What were the archive candidate totals, exclusion counts, and exclusion reasons?
- Were all candidate cases within the eight-year period reviewed, and were slides and
  clinical data reassessed?
- Was there pathologist adjudication, and how should it be described?
- What exactly do the `lymphomonocytes` low/medium/high categories represent?
- Are validated inflammatory-cell, fiber-type, denervation, fibrosis, necrosis, or
  pathology-severity estimates available with a defensible method and provenance?
- Should the new label-free correlation heatmap replace Figure 1F or become a new
  main/supplementary panel?
- What final co-last author order and equal-contribution wording should be used?

# Caveats and interpretation boundaries

- The cohort has 73 samples from 72 patients and several small disease groups.
- Disease group is structurally aligned with source, Sentrix, demographic, and biopsy-
  site variables; association cannot be interpreted as disease causation.
- Undefined or unavailable clinical/pathology variables were neither inferred nor
  imputed.
- t-SNE preserves local neighborhoods rather than trustworthy global distances; exact
  cluster geometry should not be interpreted biologically.
- Adjusted differential and supervised-learning results remain exploratory until
  replicated in an independent, balanced external cohort.

# Deliverable locations

- Main publication candidates: `figures/main/`
- Supplementary evidence: `figures/supplementary/`
- Machine-readable results: `results/tables/`
- PCA/t-SNE coordinates: `results/coordinates/`
- Full manuscript-aligned analysis report: `reports/manuscript_analysis/`
- This reviewer-to-solution report: `reports/reviewer_revision/juliane_revision.html`
